deckName: KS3 DT · J3 Lesson 7 — Teach It To See (Teacher Deck)

slides.kicker: OUR LADY'S GRAMMAR SCHOOL · DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY
slides.heading: Teach It To See
slides.sub: Today you teach your computer to know your drawings. Then you find out how it goes wrong.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: the class is coming in, signing in and opening the class link. The lesson opens on five warm-up questions from earlier lessons. The questions mark themselves. Take the register while the class answers them.

SAY: read the two sentences on the slide aloud. Then check that every pupil is sitting beside a partner.

slides.heading: What today is about
bullets: Teach a computer to tell two things apart by giving it examples.
Say why a computer gets another person’s drawings wrong.
Show that a computer can be wrong even when it is very sure.
Say when a person should check a computer’s answer.
slides.notes: SAY: these are the four things you will be able to do by the bell. Do not explain them now. The screens teach them one at a time.

slides.heading: Part 1 · Teach it
bullets: Draw five suns in the white box. Then draw five fish.
Your computer learns from your ten drawings.
Then you test it with five new drawings.
If you are stuck, press the green button that says Stuck? Show me.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: the warm-up questions are finished and the first drawing screen is open.

SAY: draw quickly. The drawings do not need to be good. Press the yellow button after each one.

slides.heading: Part 2 · Fool it · Swap seats
bullets: Your computer has only seen your drawings.
Swap seats with the person beside you.
Your partner draws six drawings on your computer.
Then you see how many it got right.
Nobody beside you? Press Nobody is beside me.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: pupils have tested their own computers and reached the screen that asks who draws next.

SAY: swap seats with your partner now. Draw on their computer the way you always draw. Do not copy their drawings.

WATCH FOR: a pupil with no partner. That pupil presses Nobody is beside me, and the computer brings drawings from another person.

slides.heading: Part 3 · Sure and wrong
bullets: Go back to your own seat.
Draw a cat. Your computer has never seen one.
See what your computer calls your cat.
Read how sure it is.
Then you choose when a person must check its answer.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: back in their own seats after the swap.

SAY: your computer only knows suns and fish. Draw a cat and see what happens.

AFTER THIS PART: each pupil names the computer, picks its weak spot and keeps a card about it. The card is used again in Lessons 8 and 9.

slides.heading: More to try
bullets: You have your card. Now there are five extra activities.
They are optional. You can do them in any order.
You can leave an activity at any time.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: the fastest pupils have their cards, about 35 minutes into the lesson. Leave this slide up while the rest of the class finishes Parts 1 to 3.

SAY: when you have your card, choose any extra activity.

slides.heading: Three questions for the room
bullets: Why did your computer get your partner’s drawings wrong?
Why did your computer call a cat a sun or a fish?
When should a person check a computer’s answer?
slides.notes:
WHEN: about fifteen minutes before the bell. Ask the class to stop and look up.

SAY: ask each question on the slide in turn. Take two or three answers to each question. Do not give the answers yourself. The end questions ask about the same ideas.

slides.heading: Go to the end questions
bullets: Press Go to the end questions now. The button is at the top of every screen.
Your drawings are saved. You lose nothing.
Answer the five questions. Then say how the lesson went.
Press Finish. You have nothing to hand in.
slides.notes:
WHEN: ten minutes before the bell.

SAY: press Go to the end questions now, even if you are in the middle of a drawing. Your drawing is saved.
